questions.q: What is a scratch org definition file?
options: A log file generated after a scratch org is deleted
A JSON blueprint specifying a scratch org's edition, features, and settings before it's created
A backup of a scratch org's data, taken automatically
A file that lists every user who has logged into the org
questions.explain: The definition file is the JSON blueprint the CLI reads when creating a scratch org, determining its edition, enabled features, and settings before the org even exists.

questions.q: By convention, where does a project's main scratch org definition file live?
options: config/project-scratch-def.json
force-app/main/default/scratch-def.json
sfdx-project.json
.forceignore
questions.explain: By convention, the definition file lives at config/project-scratch-def.json inside a Salesforce DX project, and like the rest of the project, it belongs in version control.

questions.q: What does the `features` property inside a scratch org definition file control?
options: Which Apex classes get deployed first
The scratch org's expiration duration
A list of org features/capabilities to turn on at org creation time, such as specific licenses or capabilities
Which Dev Hub the org is created under
questions.explain: The features property lists org-level features or capabilities (like specific licenses or add-ons) that should be enabled when the scratch org is created.

questions.q: To create a scratch org that matches an existing org's exact features, settings, and licenses (an org shape), which property replaces `edition` in the definition file?
options: snapshot
adminEmail
hasSampleData
sourceOrg, set to the source org's 15-character org ID
questions.explain: Building from an org shape uses the sourceOrg property set to the 15-character org ID of the source org, in place of specifying edition directly.

questions.q: Why do real projects often keep more than one scratch org definition file?
options: The CLI requires at least two definition files to function
Different purposes call for different shapes — a lean file for fast day-to-day work versus a richer file enabling every optional feature for full integration testing
Definition files expire after one use and must be regenerated
Salesforce limits each definition file to a single feature
questions.explain: Projects commonly keep a lean definition file for quick everyday feature work and a more fully-featured one for integration testing (and sometimes a CI-specific variant), rather than one file trying to serve every purpose.
